question: If the length of a rectangle is increased by 20% and the breadth is decreased by 20%, then the percentage increase or decreases in the area of the rectangle is -
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the **successive percentage change** formula: Net Change = x + y + (x × y)/100.

Here, length increase (x) = +20 and breadth decrease (y) = −20.

Net Change = 20 − 20 + (20 × (−20))/100

Net Change = 0 − 400/100 = −4%.

The **negative sign** indicates a **percentage decrease**.

**∴ The correct answer is 4% decrease.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Percentage increase in **length** = 20%

Percentage decrease in **breadth** = 20%

**Formula Used:**

**Area of Rectangle** = Length × Breadth

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5b64dd580ac92dd27314e6811bb284b6fb03ab77dc9f6dc9ddbd42d710668adb.png] 

Let initial **Length (L)** = 100 units and initial **Breadth (B)** = 100 units.

⇒ Initial Area = 100 × 100 = 10000 sq. units.

⇒ New Length = 100 + 20% of 100 = 120 units.

⇒ New Breadth = 100 − 20% of 100 = 80 units.

⇒ New Area = 120 × 80 = 9600 sq. units.

⇒ Decrease in Area = 10000 − 9600 = 400 sq. units.

⇒ Percentage Decrease = (Decrease / Initial Area) × 100

⇒ Percentage Decrease = (400 / 10000) × 100 = 4%.

**∴ The correct answer is 4% decrease.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Same Percentage Increase and Decrease

If a value is first increased by x% and then decreased by x%, there is always a net decrease given by (x/10)² % or (x²/100)%.

Area and Perimeter of Rectangle

Area = Length × Breadth. Perimeter = 2 × (Length + Breadth). Changes in dimensions directly impact these proportional values.

Successive Percentage Application

This formula applies to any product of two variables (like Price × Consumption = Expenditure) when both components change simultaneously.</p
